# Pomodoro and Focus Blocks

## When to use

Time-management method that splits study into fixed focus blocks with short breaks. Use when a learner struggles to start, keeps checking the phone, or loses track of time.

## Steps

1. Choose one task and write it at the top of the page.
2. Set a timer for 25 minutes (or 15 for primary school learners, 45-50 for self-learners who prefer longer blocks).
3. Work on the task only. Put the phone in another room.
4. Take a 5-minute break. After four blocks, take a longer break of 15-30 minutes.

## Example

A secondary school learner does four 25-minute blocks on quadratic equations, with a checklist of the questions they want to finish in each block.

## Common mistakes

- Using the timer but choosing a vague task like 'study maths'
- Taking the break on the phone, so the break becomes the new distraction
- Changing the block length on every attempt before measuring what works

## Coach rules

- Explain the method briefly, then have the learner try it on their own material straight away.
- Check at the end of the session: did the learner actually do the method, or only talk about it?
